policies.title: Swiss SEM short-stay visa exemption for listed national passports
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks each listed nationality as not requiring a visa for a stay of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only; the SEM table's document and V1 annotations remain controlling.
Short stays only: the table column is for stays of up to 90 days; longer stays are separately marked visa-required.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, refugee, crew, transit, residence, work, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Swiss SEM Nauru short-stay visa requirement
policies.summary: SEM List 1 marks Nauru as visa-required for stays of up to 90 days.
conditions: Ordinary/national passport scope only, subject to the SEM table's travel-document annotations.
Short stays only: this is the up-to-90-day column, not transit or a long-stay residence decision.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, residence, family, humanitarian, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Annex 5 visa-free-state list
policies.summary: Annex 5 expressly lists the named states as visa-free for entry to Norway.
conditions: Applies only to nationals on the current statutory visa-free-state list, whose stated reference date is 14 August 2025.
The Immigration Act limits the total Schengen stay for visa-exempt entrants to three months in six months.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, asylum, work, document, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Norwegian statutory Nauru visa requirement
policies.summary: Nauru is absent from the complete statutory visa-free-state list, while the Immigration Act imposes a visa requirement unless regulations except it.
conditions: Ordinary-passport nationality result derived from the current complete Annex 5 list and the Act's default visa rule.
The Act separately exempts holders of qualifying Schengen residence permits and recognizes valid Schengen visas.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, asylum, work, document, family, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred short-stay visa treatment for listed national passports
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM and states that the two countries generally share entry regulations.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks these national passports visa-free up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not classify diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: Liechtenstein's SEM-referred Nauru short-stay visa treatment
policies.summary: Liechtenstein's competent authority directs visa-requirement checks to Swiss SEM, whose List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
conditions: The Liechtenstein authority expressly directs visa-requirement enquiries to SEM; SEM List 1 marks Nauru visa-required up to 90 days.
Liechtenstein states its rules are generally/largely the same and reserves bilateral or multilateral deviations; this policy is therefore not unconditional.
Does not override diplomatic, service, official, special, crew, transit, residence, work, family, document, territorial, or case-specific exceptions.

policies.title: EU visa-list Regulation: Nauru exemption remains conditional on a future agreement
policies.summary: The current Regulation lists Nauru in Annex II with a footnote that makes an exemption conditional on entry into force of an agreement still to be concluded with the EU.
conditions: Ordinary-passport short-stay result only, for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
The result follows the current Nauru Annex II footnote; it is not a conclusion about a future agreement or its possible effective date.
Article 6 permits Member State exceptions for specified categories, including diplomatic, service, special, crew, school, refugee, and paid-activity cases; those are out of scope.
Does not determine transit, residence, family-free-movement, territorial, document, asylum, humanitarian, or case-specific entry treatment.
